countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

universities.name: Nellai College of Engineering
universities.summary: Nellai College of Engineering (NCE), formerly National College of Engineering, is a self-financing Muslim minority engineering college at Maruthakulam in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu, founded in 2000 by the Manarul Huda Trust. It is affiliated to Anna University, Chennai, which awards its degrees, and is AICTE-approved for seven English-taught B.E./B.Tech programmes in 2026-27.
universities.campusLifestyle: NCE was inaugurated on 7 September 2000 and has an AICTE-approved intake of 330 across seven branches for 2026-27. The CSE department lists 200 HP computers on a 32 Mbps link; the Cyber Security and AI & DS labs list 150 computers each with firewall-configured servers. College facilities include a library, a 1,000-seat auditorium, a 60-seat canteen, indoor and outdoor games and a college bus service. An Institution of Engineers (India) student chapter runs through the AI & DS department.
universities.cityProfile: The campus address is Maruthakulam P.O., Nanguneri taluk, Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu 627151, in the far south of the state; NCE publishes no distance from the campus to Tirunelveli town. Anna University lists NCE among the affiliated colleges of its Region IV, Tirunelveli. The Tirunelveli district administration names Tirunelveli Junction as the railway station and the Veinthankulam New Bus Stand as the town's bus terminal; the nearest airport is Vagaikulam in Thoothukudi district, about 20 km from Tirunelveli, and Madurai's airport is about 170 km away. NCE runs its own buses for students and staff from several places, but does not publish routes or charges.
universities.practicalExposure: NCE is not autonomous, so the syllabus, examinations and degree rules are Anna University's. Under Anna University's Regulations 2021 for affiliated colleges, a B.E./B.Tech runs eight semesters and must be completed within fourteen; students need 75 per cent attendance to sit end-semester examinations; and industrial training or internships can earn credits. AICTE's 2026-27 approval letter makes an internship mandatory for all admitted students. Recent activities listed by NCE include an ECE industrial visit to Saksam Electronics on 25 July 2026 and a one-day full-stack development workshop run by CSE and AI & DS on 30 July 2026. The CSE department lists AICTE- and IIT-sponsored short-term training programmes and Spoken Tutorial workshops. NCE does not publish placement statistics or a list of recruiting companies with offer numbers.
universities.hostelOverview: NCE runs separate hostels for men and women, with round-the-clock security, dining halls, common study halls and prayer halls. Neither the facilities page nor the 2026-27 mandatory disclosure gives hostel or mess fees, room types or capacity, so ask the college office (04635 256420) before admission. For students admitted under Tamil Nadu's 7.5 per cent government-school reservation, the disclosure says the state pays tuition, hostel and development fees under G.O. 221 of 15 November 2021.
universities.dietarySupport: Hostel residents eat in the hostel dining halls. NCE does not publish a menu, a mess fee or whether vegetarian and non-vegetarian food are served separately. The campus canteen seats 60 students and staff, and the hostels include prayer halls.
universities.safetyOverview: NCE says its men's and women's hostels are separate and have round-the-clock security. The college website links an online grievance form and student feedback forms. Its committees page returned an error when checked on 22 October 2026, so anti-ragging committee contacts were not available there.
universities.studentSupport: Admission enquiries go to +91 83001 27171; the college office is on 04635 256420 and the principal on +91 83001 27474 (principal@nce.ac.in). NCE's disclosure lists the Tamil Nadu first-graduate tuition concession, the AICTE Tuition Fee Waiver on up to 5 per cent of seats and post-matric scholarships for SC/SCA/ST students.

faq.question: Is Nellai College of Engineering a university?
faq.answer: No. NCE is a college affiliated to Anna University, Chennai, which sets the syllabus, conducts the examinations and awards the B.E. or B.Tech degree. NCE is not autonomous. It opened in 2000 as National College of Engineering, and AICTE's records show the name Nellai College of Engineering from 2022-23.

faq.question: Is NCE a government or private college?
faq.answer: It is a private, self-financing college run by the Manarul Huda Trust of Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, and AICTE lists it as a minority institution; NCE describes itself as a Muslim minority institution. AICTE classes it as Private-Self Financing, and its tuition is the fee prescribed by Tamil Nadu's fee-fixation committee for self-financing professional colleges.

faq.question: Which programmes does NCE offer in 2026-27?
faq.answer: AICTE approves seven four-year undergraduate programmes for 2026-27: B.E. Computer Science and Engineering (90 seats), B.E. Electronics and Communication Engineering (60), B.E. Electrical and Electronics Engineering (60), B.E. Civil Engineering (30), B.E. Mechanical Engineering (30), B.E. Computer Science and Engineering (Cyber Security) (30) and B.Tech Artificial Intelligence and Data Science (30). No postgraduate or doctoral programme is on AICTE's 2026-27 list.

faq.question: Can international or NRI students apply to NCE?
faq.answer: Not on student visas. AICTE's 2026-27 approval letter shows International Students approval 'No' and NRI approval 'No' for every NCE course, so there are no foreign-national or NRI seats. Seats are filled through TNEA, which admits Indian nationals meeting its nativity or Tamil Nadu schooling rules; OCI/PIO card holders who are natives of Tamil Nadu may take part under open competition unless born abroad after 4 March 2021.

faq.question: What are the eligibility requirements for B.E./B.Tech at NCE?
faq.answer: NCE's disclosure reproduces Tamil Nadu's rules: a Class 12 (HSC, +1 and +2) pass with Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry averaging at least 45 per cent for General category or 40 per cent for BC, BC Muslim, MBC & DNC and SC/SCA/ST applicants. An HSC vocational-stream pass in an engineering group with the same averages also qualifies. Diploma holders and B.Sc. Mathematics graduates may enter the third semester through lateral entry.

faq.question: How do I apply to NCE?
faq.answer: Apply online through Tamil Nadu Engineering Admissions (TNEA) at tneaonline.org; the fee is INR 500, or INR 250 for SC/SCA/ST. Upload your marksheets and certificates, then in your counselling round enter college code 4961 with your branch choices and confirm the allotment. For 2026, registration closed on 5 June and general counselling ran 20 July to 30 August. NCE publishes no separate management-quota route; its admission line is +91 83001 27171.

faq.question: What are NCE's fees?
faq.answer: NCE does not publish an amount. Its 2026-27 disclosure says tuition for every branch is the fee prescribed by the Government of Tamil Nadu's fee-fixation committee for self-financing professional colleges, and hostel, mess and bus charges are not published. Ask the college office for the current figures before you accept a seat.

faq.question: Are there fee concessions or scholarships?
faq.answer: NCE's disclosure lists four: the state pays tuition, hostel and development fees for students admitted under the 7.5 per cent government-school reservation; a first-graduate tuition concession; the AICTE Tuition Fee Waiver on up to 5 per cent of seats for family income below INR 8 lakh, with no change of college or course allowed; and post-matric scholarships for SC/SCA/ST students with family income below INR 2.5 lakh.

faq.question: What is the medium of instruction?
faq.answer: English. Anna University's Regulations 2021 for affiliated colleges make English the medium for all courses, examinations, seminar presentations and project reports, except programmes the university offers in Tamil medium; none of NCE's AICTE-approved courses is a Tamil-medium course.

faq.question: When do first-year classes start?
faq.answer: NCE follows Anna University's calendar for non-autonomous affiliated colleges. For 2026-27, first-semester B.E./B.Tech classes begin on 2 September 2026, after TNEA general counselling from 20 July to 30 August 2026. TNEA registration for 2026 closed on 5 June.

faq.question: Is NCE accredited by NBA or NAAC?
faq.answer: NCE's 2026-27 mandatory disclosure lists no NBA or NAAC accreditation. Its recognitions are AICTE approval for 2026-27 (permanent ID 1-4378723) and affiliation to Anna University, Chennai (college code 9518). The Anna University degree is the qualification you receive.

faq.question: Does NCE have hostels?
faq.answer: Yes. NCE has separate hostels for men and women with round-the-clock security, dining halls, common study halls and prayer halls, plus a 60-seat canteen on campus. It does not publish room types or hostel and mess fees, so ask the college office (04635 256420) for them.

evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival.
